<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope contains only standard variable definitions and array assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver` (hardcoded as `1.12.0`), `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. There are no top-level command substitutions, no `eval` calls, no network requests, no file system modifications, and no calls to dangerous utilities. 

Since `pkgver` is hardcoded and no `pkgver()` function is defined, no dynamic computation occurs at sourcing time. All potentially notable behavior — creating `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, running `pnpm install`, running `pnpm run build`, and copying files into `$pkgdir` — is confined to the `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions, which `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does not execute.

Sourcing this PKGBUILD to print its source info is safe.
</details>
